description: No-RAG vs Graph-RAG comparison run against locally hosted open-source models (Ollama, http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions, OpenAI-compatible endpoint, no API key). Replaces the GPT-4o/Gemini rows in the paper's model-comparison table, for which no API key is available in this environment. Reproduce with e.g. `python tasks/t1_clinical_decision_accuracy.py --dataset data/alzbench/t1/mcq.json --model llama3.2:latest --base-url http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions --mode graph_rag`.

qwen3:latest.note: thinking-enabled by default; ChatClient falls back to the reasoning trace when the visible answer is truncated and gives local calls a 1536-token floor to accommodate it

excluded.qwen3:235b-a22b: Available locally (142GB Q4_K_M MoE) but impractical for this evaluation: a single trivial one-token test took ~4 minutes including cross-GPU load and still did not finish its reasoning trace within a 20-token budget. Not run for the full item set.

bug_found_and_fixed_during_this_run: alzgraph/common.py:option_letter() originally case-folded the whole completion and returned the FIRST standalone A/B/C/D match. That is fine for a short direct answer but silently wrong for a long chain-of-thought completion (which qwen3, a thinking-enabled model, produces once it runs out of its answer budget and ChatClient falls back to the raw reasoning trace): the lowercase article 'a' folds to 'A' and gets matched before the model's actual, later conclusion. This first surfaced as an implausible T3 Graph-RAG accuracy of 0.5 (vs. 0.3 No-RAG) built mostly out of spurious 'A' extractions; spot-checking the raw traces confirmed it. Fixed to prefer the LAST explicit 'answer/option/choice is/might be X' phrase (robust to a model second-guessing itself) and fall back to the last case-sensitive bare letter otherwise. T3 Graph-RAG corrected to 0.20; T1 MCQ, T4, and the No-RAG numbers were unaffected (already short, direct completions or, for T4, an unchanged answer under the corrected extractor).
